title: The world’s ice is in real peril from climate change – and will keep melting even if we reach net zero
paragraphs: In 2015, the world agreed to work to hold climate change below 1.5°C. But that goal is no longer possible.

Earth will pass 1.5°C by 2030. Some years are already over 1.5°C warmer than the pre-industrial average. This means we are set for climate overshoot – heading for even more dangerous levels of climate change.

Are there ways of temporarily going past 1.5°C and then pulling carbon dioxide back out of the atmosphere to return us to a safer temperature? In a September report, experts from the United Nations Environment Programme point out this would rely on sustained net-negative emissions, likely to be slow and uncertain.
